title: Affine PGL actions and the canonical invariant spectrum
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $E$ a commutative $k$-algebra, $r\geq1$, and $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$ over $k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Use the test schemes, matrix groups and field tests of [def-sfb-pgl-linearized-polarization]. An affine $\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$-action on $U$ consists of left actions $a_T:\operatorname{GL}_r(\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T))\times\operatorname{Mor}_k(T,U)\to\operatorname{Mor}_k(T,U)$, natural under every morphism of test schemes $T/k$, satisfying the unit and multiplication laws, with scalar matrices acting identically. No line module or linearization is part of these data. Equivalently these are actions of the fppf quotient group sheaf $\operatorname{GL}_{r,k}/\mathbf G_{m,k}$. For $x:T\to U$, evaluation $\mathrm{ev}_x:E\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ is pullback of functions using the canonical $E\simeq\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Define the invariant subring $I=\bigcap_{T,g,x}\operatorname{Eq}(\mathrm{ev}_{a_T(g,x)},\mathrm{ev}_x)\subseteq E$; this is the scheme coaction equalizer $E^G=\{e:\rho(e)=e\otimes1\}$. The specified coefficient map $k\to E$ has image in $I$, so restrict it to $k\to I$. Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}I$ over $k$ using this restriction. The canonical quotient arrow $p:U\to Y$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(I\hookrightarrow E)$; its composite with $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the given structure map of $U$. For an algebraic space $B/k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], a map $f:h_U\to B$ is invariant when $f_T(a_T(g,x))=f_T(x)$ for every test scheme $T$, matrix $g$ and point $x$. All coefficient rings and test schemes use a common universe $u$, with categories in $u+1$.
